title: Open cluster Haffner 18
caption: The open star cluster Haffner 18, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Three stages of star formation share this frame. At the center is Haffner 18, whose mature stars have already cleared away the nebulae they were born in. At the lower left of the cluster sits a very young star still wrapped in its birth cocoon of gas. Toward the right corner, dust clouds are active stellar nurseries that will make more stars in the future.
The one scene covers the past, present and future of star birth. Haffner 18 is an open cluster of about 50 stars, several of them massive and short-lived.

The young massive star with the cryptic name FM3060a still sits inside a small, dense hydrogen shell. That shell measures about 2.5 light-years across and is growing at 20 km/s. It must have formed some 40,000 years ago.

understand.summary: FORS2 on ESO's Very Large Telescope recorded Haffner 18 through B, V, R and I filters in visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The I filter records near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the telescope gathers far more light than the eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The cluster lies between 25,000 and 30,000 light-years away. The picture was made with the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope through B, V, R and I filters, and it is credited to ESO.
alt: A cluster of mature stars at the center, a young star wrapped in gas at its lower left and dust clouds toward the right corner.
